verdict.summary: You can create a User OAuth General app and connect your own Zoom account within minutes using development credentials. Sharing it with other members of your own Zoom account needs no review but is capped at 10 or 100 installs. Letting anyone outside your account connect means passing Zoom's App Review: a functional check, then a security review (technical design docs, OWASP-based testing), plus per-scope justification, domain verification and a test plan.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for Gate 1; 1-3 days to prepare docs, listing, test plan and security info for publishing
verdict.approval_wait: About 1-3 weeks (reported). An older Zoom blog post gives a 72-hour first-response SLA, and a forum reply says the security review can take up to 2 weeks.

gates.name: Development credentials / Add App Now on your own account
gates.unlocks: You can authorize the app on your own Zoom account with the development client ID and secret, and test through Composio.
limits: You must be the account owner or an admin, or have the 'Zoom for developers' role
Free accounts must add a credit card or submit Zoom's sanctions-compliance form
Development and production credentials are separate pairs

gates.name: Private app (shared within your account) / Beta app (external sharing with Zoom approval)
gates.unlocks: Other users in your own Zoom account can authorize the app through a shared authorization URL. A beta app can be shared with external users only after Zoom approves the request.
limits: Private apps work only for members of your own Zoom account and cannot be published
Private account-level app: at most 10 additions. Private user-level app: at most 100 additions (extended authorization URLs count too)
External beta sharing needs Zoom approval: a Technical Design section, SSDLC documentation, SAST/DAST scanner output, a privacy policy, 3 of 5 additional security policies, and TLS 1.2+
A beta authorization URL is valid for 4 weeks, with up to two 4-week extensions. After that, new users cannot add the app
While a beta URL is active, you may not publicize the app or use Zoom branding
gates.time_to_reach: Immediate inside your account. External beta: 3-4 business days for Zoom to reply, plus time to prepare security documents.

gates.name: Published app (Listed or Unlisted)
gates.unlocks: Any Zoom user can install the app: from Marketplace search (Listed) or from a direct install link (Unlisted).
limits: Listed and Unlisted apps both need the full App Review: submission completeness and branding, functionality/usability/compliance, then security review
Unlisted apps still need complete listing metadata
Every domain in your URL fields needs one-time domain verification
Customer admins may need to pre-approve the app before their users can add it
Updates and new scopes are reviewed again, and users must reauthorize

steps.title: Confirm you have developer permissions on your Zoom account
steps.detail: Sign in at marketplace.zoom.us. You need to be the account owner, an account admin, or hold the 'Zoom for developers' role. An admin grants that role under User Management > Roles > Role Settings > Advanced features. On a free account, either add a credit card (Free with Credit Card) or submit Zoom's developer/entity form for U.S. sanctions compliance.
steps.est_time: 5 min (longer if you have to wait for an admin)
gotchas: The Marketplace shows the Developer link only if your account has developer permissions.

steps.title: Create a General app
steps.detail: In the Marketplace, open Developer > Created apps > Develop > Build an app, and choose General app. This is the User OAuth app type. Do not choose Server-to-Server OAuth.
gotchas: Zoom has merged the old OAuth, Chatbot and Meeting SDK app types into General app.

steps.title: Choose Admin-managed or User-managed
steps.detail: Admin-managed apps are added by account admins and can reach account-wide data, depending on scopes. User-managed apps are added by individual users and see only that user's data. Most agents that act for one user should be User-managed.
gotchas: This choice limits which scopes and features you can use.
Scopes ending in :admin require the installing user to be an admin or owner. Scopes ending in :master can only be granted to account-level apps by account owners.

steps.title: Set the OAuth redirect URL and allow list
steps.detail: Under the app's OAuth information, set the OAuth Redirect URL and add the same URL to the OAuth allow list. Both fields are required. Strict Mode and Subdomain check are optional settings that tighten URL matching.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Loopback and development URLs work for testing but may be rejected at Marketplace review.

steps.title: Pick minimal granular scopes and write a justification for each
steps.detail: Under Scopes, add only the granular scopes your agent actually uses, and mark each one required or optional. An agent can draft the description Zoom requires for each scope explaining why it is needed. Composio's default list has 26 scopes, so trim it to what your tools call.
gotchas: Zoom's Security Review team may reject scopes it judges unnecessary.
Redundant scopes get flagged, e.g. a read-only scope when you already request a broader scope that includes it.

steps.title: Connect your own account through Composio with development credentials
steps.detail: Copy the development Client ID and Client Secret into your Composio Zoom auth config (authorize URL https://zoom.us/oauth/authorize, token URL https://zoom.us/oauth/token). Then authorize, or use Add App Now > Allow in the Marketplace, to check that the flow works for your own account.
gotchas: An 'Invalid client_id' error (code 4702) means the client ID is wrong or belongs to the other credential pair (development vs. production).

steps.title: Share the private app with colleagues in your account
steps.detail: Generate the authorization URL from the app page and send it to members of your own Zoom account. No review is needed.
gotchas: Caps: 10 additions for an account-level app, 100 for a user-level app.
Private apps cannot be shared outside your account or published.

steps.title: (Optional) Request external beta sharing
steps.detail: Only if you need external testers before publishing. First complete the Technical Design section and upload SSDLC documentation, official SAST and DAST scanner output, a privacy policy, and any 3 of these 5: pen-test summary, security policy, incident response policy, vulnerability management procedures, infrastructure/dependency policy. Then submit the beta share request.
steps.est_time: 1-2 days preparation + 3-4 business days for Zoom to reply
gotchas: An approved URL lasts 4 weeks, with at most two 4-week extensions.
You cannot publicize the app or use Zoom branding while the beta URL is active.
Beta apps cannot be published until you enable publishing.

steps.title: Draft and host publishing documents on your own domain
steps.detail: An agent can draft these: a privacy policy, terms, a support page (support hours, first-response SLA, contact channels), and user documentation covering how to add, use and remove the app, including what happens to user data after removal. Host all of them on domains your company owns.
gotchas: Google Drive or Dropbox links are not accepted.
You must provide ongoing user support yourself. Zoom support does not cover your app.

steps.title: Implement the deauthorization endpoint
steps.detail: Set a Deauthorization Notification Endpoint URL. When a user removes the app, Zoom POSTs a Deauthorization Event Notification to that URL, and your endpoint should revoke the token (revocation endpoint: zoom.us/oauth/revoke).
gotchas: Reviewers test the deauthorization and app-removal flow.

steps.title: Verify every domain used in the app's URL fields
steps.detail: On the publish page, verify each domain in the privacy policy, terms, OAuth redirect, webhook and home URL fields. Use a DNS TXT record, an uploaded HTML file, a homepage meta tag, or manual approval from Zoom support.
gotchas: Your redirect URL is Composio's domain, which you cannot verify yourself. You may need manual approval from Zoom support or a callback on your own domain.

steps.title: Complete Technical Design, listing assets, test plan and test account
steps.detail: An agent can draft these: the Technical Design and security sections, the short description (150 characters or less), a detailed long description, and a test plan with step-by-step instructions for each scope, attached in the release notes field. You supply 2-3 images at 1200x780 px and a seeded test account in Test account and credentials, with one login per user role.
gotchas: Unlisted apps still need full listing metadata, or they fail review.
Your landing page must let logged-out users sign in and then authorize.
Use the 'From your landing page' add option if you want installs limited to your own customers.

steps.title: Switch to production credentials and submit for review
steps.detail: Choose Listed or Unlisted and an activation option: activate immediately after approval, or activate manually later. Submit using the production client ID, and put the production client ID and secret into your Composio auth config. If you started as a beta app, first go to Activation > Share your app with others > Change Now > Enable Publishing.
gotchas: A first submission must use the production client ID. Later update submissions use the development client ID.

steps.title: Wait for functional and security review, then fix anything flagged
steps.detail: Zoom first checks submission completeness and branding, then functionality and compliance, then security (OWASP Top 10, web scanning, manual misuse testing, vulnerable-library checks). If the app fails, Zoom uses a remediation process. After launch, adding scopes triggers another review and users must reauthorize.
gotchas: A clear test plan and well-defined scopes shorten the review.
Zoom can pull a published app while you fix serious security issues.

requirements.item: Account owner, admin, or 'Zoom for developers' role
requirements.detail: Needed to see the Developer link and build apps.
Upgrade to Free with Credit Card, or submit Zoom's developer/entity form.

requirements.item: OAuth redirect URL and allow list
requirements.detail: Both fields are required. Loopback and dev URLs may be rejected when you publish.
Each scope needs a description. Zoom's Security Review team may reject unnecessary scopes.

requirements.item: Security documentation for external beta sharing
requirements.detail: Technical Design, SSDLC, SAST/DAST output, privacy policy, 3 of 5 additional policies, TLS 1.2+.
Every domain in the privacy, terms, redirect, webhook and home URL fields.

requirements.item: Privacy policy, terms, support and documentation URLs on company-owned FQDNs
requirements.detail: The support page must list hours and a first-response SLA. Documentation must cover adding, using and removing the app.

requirements.item: Technical Design section and security information
requirements.detail: Without them the submission fails the completeness check.
2-3 images at 1200x780 px, short description of 150 characters or less, detailed long description. Required even for Unlisted apps.
Steps for each scope and a login for each user role. Required for every submission, including resubmissions.
Receives Zoom's Deauthorization Event Notification. Your app should then revoke the token.

requirements.item: Production client ID for the first submission
requirements.detail: Updates use the development client ID.

scopes.effect: Core meeting scopes. Like every scope, each needs a justification and test steps. Zoom does not publish a sensitive-scope tier.
Included in Composio's defaults. Zoom does not list these as sensitive. Request them only if your agent uses them: every extra scope makes review more intensive, and unused scopes may be removed.
Admin scopes require the installing user to be an admin or owner. Master scopes can only be granted to account-level apps by account owners.
Reviewed again if it grants access to new data. Users must reauthorize; include_granted_scopes keeps previously granted scopes in the new token.

blockers.symptom: No Developer link in the Marketplace
blockers.fix: Ask an admin to grant the 'Zoom for developers' role under User Management > Roles > Role Settings > Advanced features.

blockers.symptom: Scope request rejected or removal requested
blockers.cause: Missing justification or test steps, or the scope is redundant or unused.
blockers.fix: Request only the minimum scopes. Write a justification and test steps for each one.

blockers.cause: Listing metadata missing on the assumption that Unlisted apps don't need it.
blockers.fix: Supply full images, descriptions and categories.

blockers.cause: Documents hosted on Google Drive or Dropbox, or no support page with an SLA.
blockers.fix: Host everything on domains your company owns and verify those domains.

blockers.cause: Loopback or development URL used in production.
blockers.fix: Use a production redirect URL on a domain that can be verified.

blockers.symptom: New users can't add the private app
blockers.cause: Private app install cap reached (10 account-level, 100 user-level).
blockers.fix: Publish the app through review, or request beta sharing.

blockers.symptom: Beta testers can no longer add the app
blockers.cause: Beta authorization URL expired (4 weeks plus at most two extensions).
blockers.fix: Enable publishing and submit for review. Users who already added it keep access.

blockers.cause: Logged-out users cannot authenticate and then authorize.
blockers.fix: Make the landing page handle sign-in before starting the OAuth flow.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed Zoom OAuth app to prototype with your own or a test account. It requests 26 granular scopes, including transcript read and delete. Register your own General app when you need your own branding on the consent screen, a trimmed scope set, or distribution to other Zoom accounts. Your own app works for you at once with development credentials, but reaching other accounts requires Zoom's App Review. Paste the redirect URL shown in your Composio auth config into both the OAuth Redirect URL field and the allow list.

open_questions: No current official install cap was found for published or unlisted apps before review. The 10/100 caps apply to private apps; an older community post cites 20/200 Publishable URL caps, which conflicts.
Zoom publishes no list of sensitive scopes. It is unconfirmed whether recording or transcript scopes, such as cloud_recording:delete:meeting_transcript, add review burden.
No current official end-to-end review SLA was found. The 72-hour first-response figure comes from an older blog post, and the 2-week security review figure from a forum reply.

Domain verification covers the OAuth redirect domain. With Composio's callback URL you cannot verify that domain yourself, so it is unclear whether Zoom support's manual approval or your own callback domain is needed.
It is not documented whether Composio's managed Zoom app has passed Zoom Marketplace review.
Business verification and paid-plan requirements for publishing were not documented beyond the free-account compliance rule.
Content requirements for the privacy policy were not found.
Community posts mention a limit on how many apps can be created per 24 hours; the current figure is unconfirmed.
